rulings.by: gandalf (conductor, DRIFT-CRITIC on own C-2 derivation)
rulings.topic: GEOMETRY: the R-43 E-frame construction (staff in the FAR hand; strap from behind the neck; bare near shoulder) is the W geometry applied to E — a near/far inversion; P2 uses the R-15 DERIVED table (C-1 k2_facing_table_derived.json) extended to N
rulings.ruling: Physics (right = front × up): a right-handed figure facing screen-right presents her RIGHT side to the camera, so on E the staff is in the NEAR hand and the satchel (left hip) is on the FAR side. Evidence: (1) C-1 K2-jdg-04 (judged against the R-15 derivation) — E-c1, NE-c1, SE-c1 staff NEAR, W/NW/SW staff FAR, none mirrored; (2) the C-2 brief K2p-gen-E text says ‘only its left side is visible’ for E and the K2p-jdg-E brief says ‘she faces screen-right, so her LEFT side is NEAR’ — both inverted; (3) conductor view of k2p_E_r2 beside master C: near arm hangs empty, staff in the far hand ⇒ the staff is in her LEFT hand — Matt’s R-43 question (‘isn’t the E seed holding the staff in the wrong hand?’) was CORRECT and the C-2 judge was handed an inverted derivation. R-43’s satchel/strap text is correct for W, not E. Charter § 2/§ 3 E and § 11 cite R-43 as the judge geometry; applying it would mint mirrored bodies on 3–4 directions, violating fork E’s own clause (all 8 real, no mirroring, F3). Ruling: P2 briefs and the P2 JUDGE use the derived table (runs/C-3/k2c_facing_table.json, conductor data), with a mirrored control drawn from a generated candidate.
rulings.consequence: (a) All 7 P2 directions are generated against the derived geometry, with the C-1 K2 v4 frames as GEOMETRY-ONLY references (old register; face/brushwork not to be copied). (b) The passed C-2 walk-E exemplar (from r2) carries a mirrored staff hand — irrelevant to its motion band (R-50/R-55 stand), recorded for C-4. (c) FLAG FOR MATT at C-4 (packet 20 front page): veto-open — if Matt rules R-43 as intended (staff far on E), P2 E/NE/SE are re-minted at ≤ 6 images and their 15 clips re-driven.
rulings.evidence: runs/C-1/k2_facing_table_derived.json; runs/C-1/artifacts/K2-jdg-04/judgment.json; briefs/K2p-gen-E.task.json; briefs/K2p-jdg-E.task.json; C-1 ledger R-15, R-43

rulings.topic: SEQUENCING: P2 (turnaround) runs BEFORE P1 (T3 tooling); P3 Grok clips run DURING P1; nothing is MEASURED before its instrument is frozen
rulings.ruling: Charter § 4 lists P1 before P2 and the restart prompt says ‘T3 serial … then P2–P6’. P2 depends on no T3 instrument (GENERATE + JUDGE by rubric + PACK with frozen tools), and P3 clips are conductor-driven Grok calls, not Astra bursts, so they may run while T3 TOOLING bursts hold the lane. The Grok matrix (40+ sequential clips) is the run’s long pole; running it during T3 saves ≈ 2 h without touching any gate, band, budget or bar. Instrument-before-candidate is honoured at the MEASUREMENT boundary: no P4 cut/check runs on any clip until T3a–T3d are frozen; the head-down first-second check (charter § 6 re-generate-once rule) is applied with the T3c head-pitch proxy after T3c, and flagged clips are re-driven then. TOOLING stays serial and never overlaps a burst: P2 bursts finish (or their wave closes) before T3a launches.
rulings.consequence: Order: P2 GENERATE wave (7) + S clips from master C in parallel → P2 JUDGE (+ retries) → T3a… serially while P3 clips for the other 7 directions run → P4 after the T3d freeze.

rulings.topic: PROMPTS: matrix prompts frozen as data (runs/C-3/matrix_prompts.json, 40 cells); the cast surge reduced to a small tip glint so the plate stays empty
rulings.ruling: Charter § 6 prescribes both ‘plate unchanged and empty’ and, for cast, ‘a surge gathers at the astrolabe/tip’. A baked surge would put light and particles on the #00ff00 plate (matte contamination, R-53 family) and double the frost bolt that P5 composites at the staff-tip socket. The starter staff carries no astrolabe (bible v0.3; the astrolabe head is the ADVANCED set, R-31). Cast prompt = raises the staff two-handed, a small brief pale glint at the tip (nothing leaves the staff), thrusts forward in the facing direction, returns to rest. Every prompt carries the R-51 gaze line and names the staff hand/satchel hip (anatomical). Idle/walk keep the C-2 passed wording (idle ‘a third bigger than life’; walk treadmill + two bobs per stride); run/jump per charter § 6.
rulings.consequence: The cast one-shot is measured on the staff-tip trajectory (T3a); the VFX is P5’s. Prompt sha256 per cell ledgered in grok_calls[].
rulings.evidence: runs/C-3/matrix_prompts.json; charter § 6; C-1 R-31, R-51, R-53

rulings.topic: ONE-SHOT RE-DRIVE (method within hypothesis): all 16 jump/cast clips re-driven from PADDED seeds (70 % height, 353 px headroom) with a v2 cast prompt (staff visible in every frame, both hands, no glowing hand) and a v2 jump line (whole body and staff stay inside the frame); Grok clip count rises to ≈ 56
rulings.ruling: The R-C3-6 failure is source framing (figure ≈ 95 % of frame height ⇒ apex and staff raise exit the frame) and, for cast, clip content (staff vanishes). Two-attempt rule scope guard: this is a method change within the hypothesis (seed geometry + prompt wording), never medium. Seeds: runs/C-3/artifacts/K2c-pad/pad_<D>.png — the judged rest still cropped to its alpha bbox, uniformly downscaled to 1075 px on a 1024×1536 #00ff00 canvas, feet at row 1428 (C-1 seed.py precedent: uniform scale + translation only); pad_seeds.json records scale/paste/sha256. Prompts: matrix_prompts.json cells <D>_jump_v2 / <D>_cast_v2 (sha256 recorded). Idle/walk/run keep their full-height clips (their motion stays inside the frame; the run clips are checked for exits at P4). Budget: charter H says ~45 Grok clips with halts counting FAILURES, not clips; 40 + 16 = 56 is an estimate overage on a subscription surface with no printed cost (T30), recorded here veto-open.
rulings.consequence: 16 clips <D>_{jump,cast}_v2 generated STAGED during T3b; v1 clips kept for lineage. P4 cuts one-shots from v2; if v2 detection still fails, fallback = conductor-explicit key-pose indices from a contact sheet (R-46 precedent), flagged.

rulings.topic: T3b ACCEPTED-WITH-FINDING + FROZEN — clamp edge mode works (alpha byte-identical, rim −4.2 native); the known-bad reproduction is MARGINAL (unpremultiply 4.81 vs > 5 native; 0.09 registered); a residual light contour baked into OPAQUE edge pixels remains on dark garments (finding F-C3-1)
rulings.ruling: Receipt DELIVERED_WITH_CONCERNS (audit clean; 9 min, 16 calls); suite 223/217 (same six standing reds); regression lock 1880 comparisons within tolerance. Real frames (16 native idle_C frames): unpremultiply rim_luma_excess mean 4.81 (min 1.05, max 8.05) vs the pre-registered > 5 — MISSED by 0.19; clamp −4.18 (≤ 5 ✓); alpha area lost 0.0 % (byte-identical ✓); registered scale: unpremultiply 0.09, clamp −8.26. Synthetic soft disc: 10.9 vs 7.4 ✓. Conductor eye on edge_crops (frame 1, ×4 enlarged): unpremultiply shows a pale rim on the sleeve and a light line along the trouser contour; clamp reduces both but a faint light contour persists on the navy trousers — those pixels are classified OPAQUE (source video edge bleed), so no partial-alpha edge mode can reach them. Disposition: NOT a burst FAIL — the contracted mechanism is built and behaves as specified; criterion (1) was a conductor expectation about the metric’s discrimination that the data only marginally supports. Rubric law (desirable-run-pattern § 6.3): rim_luma_excess does NOT answer Matt’s question (‘is the white glow gone’) and is reported, never gated. Matt’s eye at C-4 rules the residual contour; R-55 recorded ‘no matte/glow’ on the Lanczos encode of cut B, so the visible glow is partly encode-dependent (T3d).
rulings.consequence: P4 cuts with --edge-mode clamp. F-C3-1 goes on the C-4 front page (residual contour on dark cloth; candidate next-lap levers: a 1-px opaque-edge despill toward the interior colour, or premultiplied compositing at the engine). Freeze recorded below; T3c fires.
